title: Developer Promise — variants + test matrix
content:
Objective:
Provide a compact set of distinct homepage hero variants and downstream product copy that directly map to three developer purchase triggers: (1) predictable latency & reliability, (2) unit-economics control, (3) safe/private compliance. We will run staged A/B experiments measuring sign-up conversion and API key creation + quickstart calls.

Audience segments (priority order):
1) Mid-stage startups (~10–200 engs) building LLM features into product flows; care about cost predictability and fast time-to-market.
2) Platform/infra teams at larger orgs who want standardized inference runtime and rollout control.
3) Regulated customers (health/finance/enterprise) needing private deployments & auditability.

Working hypothesis:
- Hyp A: Developers convert more when hero language emphasizes "predictable inference economics" + an immediate interactive demo.
- Hyp B: Platform engineers respond better to a technical-first hero (latency SLOs, traceable rollouts) with a CTA to benchmarking docs.
- Hyp C: Compliance-focused buyers need an explicit privacy-first hero with clear deployment options (VPC/on-prem) and KMS badges.

Hero/tagline variants (short, test-ready):
Variant 1 — Predictable: "Make inference predictable: latency, cost, and uptime you can build on."
Variant 1 subhead: "Unified runtime for hosted, dedicated, or private deployments — ship LLM features without the economics surprise."
CTA options: "Try a cost-first demo", "Estimate token price"

Variant 2 — Performance-first: "Low-latency inference engineered for production scale."
Variant 2 subhead: "GPU-optimized serving, smart routing and graceful fallbacks that keep product flows snappy."
CTA options: "Run a latency test", "See performance benchmarks"

Variant 3 — Trust/Privacy: "Keep model serving private where it matters."
Variant 3 subhead: "VPC, on‑prem options, and auditable keys — enterprise controls with dev ergonomics."
CTA options: "Request private trial", "Security brief"

Downstream product headlines (short blurb for product cards):
- Redwood API: "Simple API for generation, chat and embeddings with transparent performance profiles."
- Dedicated: "Reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed throughput and burst options."
- Private: "Customer-controlled deployments — network isolation, KMS/HSM, and audit logs."
- Optimize: "Guided batching, cache and quantization recommendations to lower unit costs."

Proof points / trust signals to test on-page: (each item as A/B toggle)
- Measured claims: "P95 latency under 120ms for common LLMs (public benchmark)"
- Cost claim: "Typical per-token savings of 30% via auto-batching & prefix caching"
- Enterprise badges: "SOC 2 Type II review in progress" (test phrasing: "in progress" vs "available")
- Customer quote (placeholder): "We cut inference cost while improving latency — platform-level controls made rollout safe." — Customer X (SaaS)

Competitive differentiator notes (quick bullets to feed copy/legal):
- Not just model access: emphasize serving primitives (batching, KV-caching, routing) that materially change unit economics vs simple endpoints.
- Unified surface: same API and rollout controls across hosted -> dedicated -> private; messaging should use the word "same API" and "same defaults".
- Fallback and graceful degradation: call out automatic fallback to compatible model variants during capacity constraints — positions Redwood as reliability-first.

Risks / messaging landmines to avoid:
- Avoid claiming specific SLAs for hosted (we offer SLA for Dedicated only).
- Don’t overpromise quantization savings as exact numbers — phrase as "typical" or "empirically observed".
- Be careful with "open model catalog" phrasing — clarify Redwood-curated and verified models to avoid legal/model licensing confusion.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Primary metric: developer sign-ups that create API key and make a first successful generation call within 24 hours.
- Secondary metrics: docs click-through, benchmark test runs, demo interactions, enterprise contact submissions.
- Variants: hero copy (3), CTA framing (demo vs estimate vs docs), trust signals presence (badges on/off), lead magnet (cost calculator vs latency demo).
- Sample traffic plan: 4-week runway, start with even traffic split across hero copy variants (n ≈ 2k unique visitors per arm), funnel measurement weekly, shortlist winning variant by week 3.

Conversion hypotheses per segment: 
- Startups: Variant 1 + cost-calculator => higher quickstart run rate.
- Platform teams: Variant 2 + benchmarking link => higher benchmark-run and docs engagement.
- Regulated customers: Variant 3 + security brief => higher private-trial requests.

Microcopy experiments (short lines to A/B):
- API onboarding success: "Your API key is live — start a generation in seconds" vs "API key ready — try the quickstart now"
- Billing microcopy: "Predictable billing with per-route reporting" vs "Per-route cost breakdowns to eliminate billing surprises"

Visual / layout cues to pair with copy (engineering brief):
- Variant 1: show cost-graph micro-visual (tokens vs $) and an interactive estimator input.
- Variant 2: show p95 latency graph, sequence-length waterfall and a tiny benchmark runner UI.
- Variant 3: show topology diagram (hosted/dedicated/private) and security badge strip.

Next steps & owner tasks:
- Marketing engineer: wire up three hero experiments (feature-flagged) + event goals (signup, api-first-call) — owner: Arjun Patel — due: 2026-03-15.
- Growth PM: build cost-estimator micropage and bench-run quickstart — owner: Sofia Alvarez — due: 2026-03-22.
- Legal/security: verify badge language and private-deploy copy — owner: Leo Martins — due: 2026-03-12.

Notes and open questions (brainstorm fragments):
- Should we surface a simple "cost per 1k tokens" starter benchmark or only an interactive estimator? (tradeoff: anchoring vs precision)
- Is it worth a separate landing flow for Private vs folding into a single product page? (data: enterprise traffic low but high LTV)
- Do we show competitor logos in a "who we outperform" grid? needs legal check.

Raw copy snippets (for quick paste into AB tool):
- "Predictable inference that scales with your product, not your spend"
- "Ship LLM features with SLAs, cost controls, and the same API across deployments"
- "Keep inference local where it matters — private hosting, audited keys, operator-friendly rollouts"

Status: draft playbook for experimentation. Feedback requested from product, security, and growth before flagging to web engineering for implementation.

Attachments / references: confluence:GT-landing-ux-brief-2025 (detailed wireframes), jira:GT-1128 (web A/B infra), github:repo/marketing/PR-74 (asset pack).

Document author: Maya Chen — PT notes: focus on measurable CTAs (demo/estimate/bench) rather than pure marketing language.
